title: Application of Integrals
description: Class 12 IMO — Application of Integrals: area under a curve, area between two curves, and areas of standard regions such as circles and parabolas.

topics.title: Area Under a Curve
topics.concept:
The definite integral computes the area between a curve and an axis. For a curve $y=f(x)$ that lies above the $x$-axis between $x=a$ and $x=b$,

$$\text{Area}=\int_a^b y\,dx=\int_a^b f(x)\,dx.$$

When the curve dips below the axis

Where $f(x)<0$, the integral returns a negative value. Since area is positive, split the interval at the $x$-intercepts and take the absolute value of each piece:

$$\text{Area}=\int_a^c f\,dx + \left|\int_c^b f\,dx\right|.$$

Area with respect to the $y$-axis

If a region is described more naturally in terms of $x=g(y)$, integrate along $y$:

$$\text{Area}=\int_c^d x\,dy=\int_c^d g(y)\,dy.$$

Always sketch the region first — the picture fixes the limits and tells you whether to integrate in $x$ or $y$.

examples.problem: Find the area under $y=x^2$ from $x=0$ to $x=3$.
Find the area bounded by $y=x^2$, the $x$-axis and $x=2$.
Find the area under $y=\sin x$ from $0$ to $\pi$.
Find the area of the region bounded by $x=y^2$ and $x=4$ (in the first quadrant).
examples.solution: Integrate along $y$ from $0$ to $2$ (since $x=4\Rightarrow y=2$): area $=\int_0^2 (4-y^2)\,dy=\left[4y-\dfrac{y^3}{3}\right]_0^2=8-\dfrac{8}{3}=\dfrac{16}{3}$ square units.

recap: Below the axis the integral is negative; split at intercepts and take absolute values.
Sketch the region first to set the correct limits.

quiz.q: The area enclosed between the curves y = x² and y = x is:
quiz.explanation: Intersection points: x² = x → x(x − 1) = 0 → x = 0, 1. Area = ∫[0 to 1] (x − x²) dx = [x²/2 − x³/3]₀¹ = 1/2 − 1/3 = 1/6 sq unit.

quiz.q: Find the area of the region in the first quadrant enclosed by the circle x² + y² = 4.
quiz.explanation: Total area = π(2²) = 4π. Area in the first quadrant = 4π / 4 = π sq units.

topics.title: Area Between Two Curves
topics.concept:
The area between two curves $y=f(x)$ (upper) and $y=g(x)$ (lower) from $x=a$ to $x=b$ is the integral of the gap between them:

$$\text{Area}=\int_a^b \big[f(x)-g(x)\big]\,dx,\qquad f(x)\ge g(x)\ \text{on }[a,b].$$

Finding the limits

The limits $a,b$ are usually the $x$-coordinates of the points of intersection, found by solving $f(x)=g(x)$. Decide which curve is on top in the region (test a sample point) so the integrand stays non-negative.

If the curves cross

When the curves swap top/bottom inside the interval, split at the crossing points and integrate each sub-interval with the correct "upper minus lower" order. The total area is the sum of these positive pieces.

examples.problem: Find the area between $y=x$ and $y=x^2$ from their intersections.
examples.solution: Intersections: $x=x^2\Rightarrow x=0,1$. On $(0,1)$, $x\ge x^2$. Area $=\int_0^1 (x-x^2)\,dx=\left[\dfrac{x^2}{2}-\dfrac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^1=\dfrac12-\dfrac13=\dfrac16$ square units.

Intersections: $x^2=4\Rightarrow x=\pm2$. Upper curve is $y=4$. Area $=\int_{-2}^{2}(4-x^2)\,dx=\left[4x-\dfrac{x^3}{3}\right]_{-2}^{2}=\left(8-\dfrac83\right)-\left(-8+\dfrac83\right)=\dfrac{32}{3}$ square units.

examples.problem: Find the area between the line $y=2x$ and the parabola $y=x^2$.
examples.solution: $x^2=2x\Rightarrow x=0,2$. On $(0,2)$, $2x\ge x^2$. Area $=\int_0^2(2x-x^2)\,dx=\left[x^2-\dfrac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^2=4-\dfrac83=\dfrac{4}{3}$ square units.

examples.problem: Set up the area between $y=\sqrt{x}$ and $y=x$ for $0\le x\le1$.

recap: Limits are the intersection points: solve $f(x)=g(x)$.
Test a sample point to decide which curve is upper.
If the curves cross, split the interval and add positive pieces.

quiz.q: Calculate the area of the region bounded by the parabolas y = 2x² and y = x² + 4.
quiz.explanation: Intersections: 2x² = x² + 4 → x² = 4 → x=±2. Area = ∫(−2 to 2) (x² + 4 − 2x²) dx = 2∫(0 to 2) (4 − x²) dx = 32/3 sq units.

quiz.q: The area bounded by the curve y = log x, the x-axis and the lines x = 1 and x = e is:
quiz.explanation: Area = ∫[1 to e] log x dx = [x log x − x]₁ᵉ = (e·1 − e) − (1·0 − 1) = 0 − (−1) = 1 sq unit.

topics.title: Areas of Standard Regions
topics.concept:
Integration recovers familiar areas: a circle x² + y² = a² has area πa², and integration gives the area of segments and parabolic regions.

Exploit symmetry to integrate over one quadrant and multiply.

examples.problem: Area of a quarter of the circle x² + y² = 9.

recap: Circle of radius a: area πa².
Use symmetry to shorten the integral.

quiz.q: A plot is in the shape of the region between y = √x, y = x. The cost of fencing at ₹50 per unit length of perimeter is approximately (use integration for arc length if needed, but area in sq units is asked here). Actually, if land price is ₹200 per sq unit, the total land cost is:
Sachin is creating a logo for the E-learning Hub Yudgam. The design involves the region bounded by y = x² and the horizontal line y = 9. What is the geometric area of this region in square units?
quiz.explanation: Intersect at x = −3, 3. Area = ∫(−3 to 3) (9 − x²) dx = 2 × [9x − x³/3] from 0 to 3 = 2 × (27 − 9) = 36 sq units.

questions.q: Find the area of the region bounded by the parabola x² = 4y and the straight line x = 4y − 2.
questions.explanation: Substitute y = (x+2)/4 into parabola: x² = x+2 → x²−x−2=0. Roots x=−1, 2. Area = ∫(−1 to 2) ((x+2)/4 − x²/4) dx = 1/4 [x²/2 + 2x − x³/3] from −1 to 2 = 9/8 sq units.

questions.q: The area of the smaller part of the circle x² + y² = a² cut off by the line x = a/√2 is:
questions.explanation: Smaller part is to the right of x = a/√2. Area = 2 ∫[a/√2 to a] √(a² − x²) dx = 2[(x/2)√(a²−x²) + (a²/2)sin⁻¹(x/a)]_(a/√2)^a = 2[0 + (a²/2)(π/2) − (a/(2√2))(a/√2) − (a²/2)(π/4)] = 2[a²π/4 − a²/4 − a²π/8] = 2[a²π/8 − a²/4] = a²π/4 − a²/2 = (a²/2)(π/2 − 1) sq units.

questions.q: For a physics demonstration at Yudgam Foundation, a student tracks a particle whose velocity curve forms a region bounded by y = |x − 3| and the x-axis from x = 0 to x = 6. What is the total distance (area)?
questions.explanation: Graph forms two right triangles of base 3 and height 3. Area = 2 × (1/2 × 3 × 3) = 9 units.

questions.q: The area of the region bounded by y = min{|x|, 1} and y = max{|x|, 1} for |x| ≤ 2 is:
What is the area of the region bounded by the curves y = √x and y = x²?
questions.explanation: Intersections at x=0, x=1. Area = ∫(0 to 1) (√x − x²) dx = [2/3 x^(3/2) − x³/3] = 2/3 − 1/3 = 1/3 sq units.

questions.q: For an odd function f(x), the integral ∫(−a to a) f(x) dx = 0. What does this imply about the geometric areas bounded by the curve and the x-axis on the intervals [−a, 0] and [0, a]?
options: They are equal in magnitude but opposite in sign.
The curve does not exist on this interval.
questions.explanation: Odd symmetry means the region below the axis perfectly mirrors the region above the axis, causing the signed areas to sum to zero.

questions.q: What is the area of the region completely bounded by the downward opening parabola y = 4x − x² and the x-axis?
questions.explanation: Roots are x=0, 4. Area = ∫(0 to 4) (4x − x²) dx = [2x² − x³/3] = 32 − 64/3 = 32/3 sq units.

questions.q: Sachin allocates a triangular plot bounded by the line y = 2x, the x-axis, and the boundary x = 10 for a local tree plantation drive. What is the plot's area in square meters?
questions.explanation: Area = ∫(0 to 10) 2x dx = [x²] from 0 to 10 = 100 sq meters.

questions.q: To compute the area between two curves f(x) and g(x) where f(x) ≥ g(x) for all x in [a, b], which integral setup is correct?
options: |∫(a to b) f(x) dx| − |∫(a to b) g(x) dx|
questions.explanation: The correct formulation for the area between curves is the integral of the upper curve minus the lower curve: ∫ (upper − lower) dx.

questions.q: The area bounded by y = log x, y = 0 and x = e is:
questions.explanation: Area = ∫[1 to e] log x dx = [x log x − x]₁ᵉ = (e−e) − (0−1) = 1 sq unit.

questions.q: The area of the region bounded by y = x² + 1, y = x, x = 0 and x = 2 is:
questions.explanation: Area = ∫[0 to 2] ((x² + 1) − x) dx = [x³/3 + x − x²/2]₀² = 8/3 + 2 − 2 = 8/3 sq units.

questions.q: Find the area bounded by the straight line y = 2x, the x-axis, and the line x = 5.
questions.explanation: Area = ∫(0 to 5) 2x dx = [x²] from 0 to 5 = 25 − 0 = 25 sq units.

questions.q: The area of the region bounded by the lines y = 2x, y = x/2 and x = 2 is:
Sachin cuts a wooden board bounded by the curve y = x³ and the line y = 8, along with the y-axis, to make an E-learning Hub sign. What is the area of the board?
questions.explanation: Integrating with respect to y: Area = ∫(0 to 8) x dy = ∫(0 to 8) y^(1/3) dy = [3/4 y^(4/3)] from 0 to 8 = 3/4 × 16 = 12 sq units.

questions.q: A student calculates ∫(0 to 2π) sin(x) dx = 0 and concludes the area bounded by y = sin(x) and the x-axis from 0 to 2π is 0. What is the correct area?
questions.explanation: Definite integral gives net signed area. True geometric area = ∫(0 to π) sin(x) dx + |∫(π to 2π) sin(x) dx| = 2 + |−2| = 4 sq units.
